units.function: Large database-backed integration suite for Paperclip's Pipeline API: definitions, stages, transitions, documents, cases, blockers, leases, review, events, issue/workspace links, conversations, automations, provenance, pagination and tenant/Agent boundaries.
units.dependencyDirection: Board or Agent actors enter Express routes; route/service policy operates over relational pipeline, case, event, document, issue, routine, automation, workspace, permission and activity tables. Stage automation creates execution issues/routine work and projects provenance back into case details.
units.keyDataModels: Pipeline/stage/transition and stage config; case/parent/blocker/fields/workspaceRef/version/lease; case event and actor/run attribution; suggestion/review decision; issue link and conversation; routine/automation execution/requestKey/attempt provenance; project and isolated execution workspace; structured conflict/error; event pagination/context pack.
units.lifecycle: Create a pipeline graph and guidance; ingest cases singly or in a forward-referencing batch; claim, mutate and transition under optimistic versioning; request and resolve transitions; block/unblock; open linked work; execute/retry stage automation with workspace validation; enter a human review stage; approve/reject/request changes; emit attributable events; expose bounded history/context and retire or migrate structures.
units.testAssessment: The 19 scenarios cover an unusually broad end-to-end surface and several production concerns: tenant-first 404s, run attribution, optimistic conflicts, atomic review edits, partial bulk success, bounded histories, automation provenance, workspace consistency and legacy compatibility. All 19 were skipped locally because embedded Postgres support was unavailable, so runtime success is unverified here. Gaps include non-admin human role/capability matrices, human reviewer qualification/delegation, grant provenance, self-escalation, pipeline graph cycles/unreachable stages, lease expiry/steal races, transition/automation idempotency keys, retry budgets/backoff/cancel, crash recovery/outbox, secret/data contracts, evidence integrity, webhook/event replay and schema migration/rollback behavior.
units.designRationale: Offer a configurable operational workflow layer above issues, preserving traceability and human review while automating repeatable stage work and remaining compatible with earlier simple automation configuration.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs configurable FDE/industry workflows and Agent Boss review without duplicating generic task/run infrastructure or reducing accountable-human approval and evidence to a board-stage transition.
units.companyOsFit: ADAPT Pipeline as the strongest current Paperclip reference for configurable workflow/FDE templates, not as Company OS responsibility authority. Separate immutable template versions from instantiated cases; preserve optimistic versions, bounded histories, exact tenant 404s, source automation lineage, workspace validation and per-item bulk results. Add a compiled graph validator, idempotent command IDs, durable outbox/event sequence, lease fencing, retry/cancel/compensation and template upgrade/migration. Bind every executable transition to Work + ResponsibilityContract + Principal + permission/data grant snapshots. Review must name a qualified human principal and bind decision, exact action/result digest, evidence, reason, policy and delegation. Data fields/workspaces/documents require authorization/export policy and retention classification.
units.responsibilityConflict: A review stage is labelled human and blocks Agent exit, but approval is not shown bound to a qualified accountable person, a responsibility contract, exact action digest, evidence or data-permission snapshot. The board actor is an implicit instance admin, Agent permission grants can lack a human grantor, and stage automation can create delegated execution work without proving organizational responsibility acceptance.

units.securityFindings: POSITIVE: broad cross-tenant operations consistently expect non-oracular 404; Agent mutation requires runId; Agent cannot leave a human-review stage; workspace/project ownership mismatch fails before work creation; optimistic versions and structured conflict details exist; histories and context are bounded; unlink events retain Agent/run attribution. CRITICAL Company OS responsibility gap: human review lacks qualified human identity, responsibility contract, action digest and evidence binding. HIGH authorization gap: most positive flows use an implicit instance-admin board actor, while the one Agent grant has no demonstrated human grantor. HIGH automation gap: no idempotency/retry budget/cancel/outbox/crash-recovery proof for stage automation or retry. HIGH data-governance gap: arbitrary fields, documents, workspace refs, reasons and context packs lack data authorization/export/retention evidence. MEDIUM concurrency gap: case versioning is covered but lease fencing, bulk interleavings and graph edits during execution are not. MEDIUM privacy gap: review reasons are retained verbatim without classification/redaction policy. TEST GAP: all database-backed scenarios were skipped locally.
